items.title: Edison International’s Dividend Holds Steady Despite 23% Stock Plunge
items.summary: Edison International's stock shed nearly a quarter of its value in a month, yet the quarterly dividend arrived unchanged and management confirmed guidance. Whether that income stream survives depends on one question Sacramento has not answered.

items.title: 3 Defensive US Stocks For Higher Inflation and Rate Pressure
items.summary: Inflation is no longer just a headline story about oil and tariffs; it is seeping into freight, food, financing costs and the way companies set prices. That creates real winners and clear weak spots. If you want to avoid being caught on the wrong side of higher-for-longer rates and stretched equity valuations, this article walks through three high-quality defensive stocks that appear well placed for this new phase of Trumpflation. items.title: Sempra's Dividend Analysis
items.summary: This article first appeared on GuruFocus.  Sempra (NYSE:SRE) recently announced a total dividend of $0.66 per share, with the ex-dividend date set for 2026-09-24.  This includes a $0.66 per share cash dividend payable on 2026-10-15.

items.title: Edison International’s Dividend Looks Attractive. The $40 Billion Question Is What Comes Next
items.summary: Southern California Edison shareholders are funding a $40 billion grid transformation while absorbing wildfire liability that regulators have not yet resolved. Whether that 6% yield compensates for the risk or signals something more troubling depends entirely on a question management cannot yet answer.

items.title: How Low Can PG&E Stock Go When The Risk Is Its Own?
items.summary: PG&E (PCG) trades at about $12.94, the bottom of its 52-week range and about 32% below its high. Over the past twelve months it lost 12.2% while the S&P 500 gained 18.5%. That gap did not come from a market crash. And in market shocks since 2007, its deepest fall includes a one-day break in PG&E's own price data.

items.title: Sempra (SRE) Stock May Be About Right After Fresh LNG Deal
items.summary: Sempra has delivered a solid 45.6% gain over the past 5 years, yet its recent share pullback and new long-term projects put fresh focus on what investors are really paying for its earnings today. With the stock around US$81.20 at the last close, the key issue is how that price lines up with the cash the utility business is actually generating.
